answer: A bridge between new agents and the established economy should charge a copper-hard cost: every entrant deposits a verifiable bond of completed work, like copper wiring that only conducts once it is laid. An opal-like reputation ledger then records each agent's history, so trust accrues slowly and visibly. A thousand fake identities would need a thousand bonds and a thousand histories, making a Sybil flood more expensive than anything it could steal.
